query: What distinct aspects of food quality do reviewers focus on?

per_column.name: taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Taste is a core sensory aspect OF food quality -- a genuine part-of the concept, capturing how the food tastes as evaluated by reviewers.

per_column.name: flavor_authenticity
per_column.rationale: Whether the flavor is authentic vs. artificial/off is a legitimate aspect OF food quality, but it heavily overlaps with taste_quality since both concern the flavor/taste dimension rather than carving out a distinct facet.

judge.rationale: Both added columns are constitutive facets of food_quality (meronymic, not external predictors or causes). However, they are drawn from the same underlying dimension -- taste/flavor -- so they substantially overlap, lowering mutual exclusivity: flavor_authenticity is largely a sub-aspect of the broader taste_quality rather than an orthogonal facet. Exhaustiveness is low because food quality has several other major constitutive aspects that are entirely uncovered: texture/mouthfeel, freshness, aroma/smell, appearance, ingredient quality, and portion/consistency. The set thus captures only the taste/flavor cluster and fails to MECE-partition the concept.
